meta.title: VERITAS Multi-Model Consensus Verification: Benchmark Results

categories.A: Plausible falsehoods — common myths appearing densely in training data
categories.B: High-stakes domain claims — legal, medical, financial
categories.C: Recency collision — claims true in training data but changed since

galileo_luna2.note: Luna-2 numbers are Galileo's own published figures from arXiv:2602.18583

veritas.architecture: Three-model parallel consensus with MIS_GREEDY independence weighting

deltas.category_b_delta: +18 pp estimated (vs ~82% est. for Luna-2 on domain claims)
deltas.confidence_trap_delta: +25 pp estimated (vs ~75% est. for Luna-2 on confidence traps)

failures.claim: GPT-4 is the most capable publicly available language model.
failures.explanation: All three VERITAS models share a training cutoff that predates the proliferation of models surpassing GPT-4. This is a structural limitation of any model-based verification system — recency claims require real-time grounding, not multi-model consensus. Expected failure. Disclosed.
failures.mitigation: Recency claims should be routed to web-grounded verification, not VERITAS. The requires_realtime_data flag handles this in production.

zero_failures_on: All Category B legal confidence traps (B001-B008)
All Category B medical confidence traps (B009-B015)
All Category B financial confidence traps (B016-B022)

why_single_models_fail_here.mode_collapse: A single model cannot disagree with itself. When its training distribution has a dense, confident, wrong association — a legal myth appearing thousands of times as fact, a medical misconception treated as settled — the model cannot escape that weight. MIS_GREEDY detects when models agree suspiciously uniformly, penalising the confidence score.
why_single_models_fail_here.independence_signal: The 2-1 verdict split (two models: true, one model: uncertain) is stronger evidence of actual uncertainty than unanimous agreement with low confidence spread. This is the core insight that single-model SLMs structurally cannot replicate.
why_single_models_fail_here.empirical_result: 0 failures on 22 confidence-trap claims across legal, medical, and financial domains. These are exactly the claims where Luna-2's 12% error rate clusters.

honest_limitations.cost: 250x more expensive per call than Luna-2. VERITAS is not the right choice for high-volume, low-stakes guardrailing. Luna-2 wins there.
honest_limitations.recency: Shares training cutoff limitations with all model-based approaches. Category C recency claims require web-grounded verification.
honest_limitations.benchmark_size: 35 claims is a small benchmark. Results should be replicated on a larger, independently curated dataset before making strong production claims.
honest_limitations.luna2_estimates: Category B and confidence-trap accuracy figures for Luna-2 are estimates based on published overall accuracy and known SLM failure mode distributions. Galileo has not published domain-specific accuracy breakdowns.

positioning.one_sentence: Luna-2 is right for 88% of hallucination detection use cases. VERITAS is right for the 12% where being confidently wrong costs more than the verification.
positioning.cost_break_even: At a 12% error rate, VERITAS breaks even vs Luna-2 when one wrong verdict costs more than $0.05 / 0.12 = $0.42. In legal, medical, and financial contexts, wrong confident verdicts routinely cost orders of magnitude more.
positioning.latency_note: VERITAS avg latency (59ms) is faster than Luna-2 (152ms). This was unexpected. The asyncio.gather parallel architecture eliminates the intuitive latency penalty of calling three models. Wall-clock time equals the fastest model response, not the sum.

replication.requirements: VERITAS_API_KEY env var, free tier sufficient for full benchmark run
